reviews.scopeMarkdown: **Số từ bài gốc: 204 từ**, đếm trên nguyên văn bằng cách tách theo khoảng trắng; đủ tối thiểu 150 từ nhưng vượt 4 từ so với giới hạn 150–200 từ của lớp. Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; không chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Bài này em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu: “Also note is that” thiếu “of”, còn vế sau “; however,” thiếu chủ ngữ. Em cũng viết sai chủ thể trong “Belgium rose significant” và đọc sai tỷ lệ phần trăm cuối kỳ của UK, dẫn đến so sánh sai với Belgium. Em đã chọn được đỉnh của France và nhóm dữ liệu có thể giữ, nhưng Overview còn thiếu thông tin thấp nhất. Đi học là để ghi chép, hiểu và vận dụng lại kiến thức vào bài tự viết. Cô yêu cầu em sửa các câu được đánh dấu và rút bài về đúng độ dài trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 so sánh ba tỷ lệ phần trăm đầu kỳ rồi tập trung vào Germany và Italy; Detail 2 triển khai France, Belgium và UK. Cô giữ cách chia này: Germany và Italy là hai nước có tỷ lệ phần trăm cao nhất vào cuối kỳ, còn France có diễn biến riêng cần làm rõ. Em cần giữ đỉnh France năm 2004 và thể hiện việc UK bằng Belgium năm 2012; không gọi Germany–Italy là nhóm dẫn đầu suốt giai đoạn.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates the percentage of female members of parliament in major European nations over 12-years period ,commencing 2000.
Overall, there was a increase in the share of female members of parliament in the most countries. Italy recorded the highest figure at the end of period, while the UK experienced the most significant growth. Also note is that France showed considerable fluctuations throughout the period of time.
To elaborate, in 2000, standing 33% Germany recorded marking the highest percentage, followed by Italy and France respectively at approximately 26% and 25%. The figure for Germany increased slightly and reached around 37% in 2012. The figure for Italy ,Likewise, saw a steady rise from 26% to 39%, becoming highest point of the entire chart.
Regarding the remaining, the figure for France increase from 25% in 2000 to a peak of 37% in 2004 before declining to around 29% in 2008 and recovering slightly to almost 30%. Meanwhile, Belgium rose significant between 17% and 28% and then remained relatively stable during the period of time. The dramatic upturn was seen in the figures for the UK from under 5% to around 24% between 2000 and 2012; however, still remained below those of the four others.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrate the main reason why students chose a particular university in 1997 and 2007.
Overall, suitable degree courses remained the most popular reason in both years. The share of students choosing a university because of its proximity to their parental home and the quality of teaching increased, while the opposite trend was seen in quality of resources and good sports and socials activities.
To elaborate, in 1997, suitable degree courses accounted for the largest proportion, at 35% followed by quality of recourses at 21%. Good sports and social activities stood at 39%, while the quality of teaching and proximity to parental home made up 15% to 10% respectively.
In term of 2007, suitable degree courses still recorded the highest figure, at 37% which was a slight increase of 2 percentages points. Proximity to parental home rose significantly from 10% to 22%, becoming the second most common reason. Likewise, the figure for quality of teaching increased between 15% and 18%. In contrast, quality of resources fell from 21% to 17% , while the god sports and social activities experienced the most significant decrease, dropping from 19% to only 6%.

Thus, the UK will still have the lowest percentage among the three countries, as it did at the earlier two points, and this pattern is clear throughout.

Overall, doctors earned more money than other workers in all seven countries. The US had the highest salaries for both groups, while Finland had the lowest salary for doctors.
To elaborate, the salaries of doctors, the US ranked first, with an annual pay of approximately $120,000. Switzerland and France had the same figure, at around $70,000. Similarly, doctors in the Czech Republic and Germany earned relatively similar salaries, at about $64,000 and $63,000, respectively. Mean while, the figures for Italy and Finland were lower, at approximately $60,000 and $50,000, respectively.
Regarding the remaining, the US also had the highest annual salary, at around $45,000, followed by Switzerland, at $40,000. In contrast, France and Finland recorded lower figures, at approximately $29,000 and $26,000, respectively. The remaining three countries, including Italy, the Czech Republic and Germany, had the same salary level, at around $20,000. It is also noticeable that the salary gap between doctors and other workers was largest in the US, at approximately $75,000.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table chart illustrates how the first year students who gave a “very good” rating to the resources provided by the college for three courses.
Overall, Commerce recorded the highest levels of satisfaction in most categories, while Law generally had lower figures. Teaching was the most highly rated aspect of Economics, whereas other resources received the highest percentage in Law.
To elaborate on this, regarding pre-course information, Commerce recorded the highest figure, at 95%, followed by Law at 72%, while Economics had the lowest percentage, at 59%. A similar trend could be seen in teaching, with Economics and Commerce sharing the highest rate of 95%, compared with only 62% for Law. In terms of tutoring, Commerce ranked first, at 93%, closely followed by Economics at 90%, whereas Law accounted for the lowest figure, at 76%.
Regarding printed resources, Commerce recorded the highest percentage, at 85%, followed by Economics at 81% and Law at 70%. A similar pattern was observed in other resources, where Commerce again ranked first, at 81%, while Law stood at 80%. Economics, by contrast, recorded the lowest figure, at just 60%.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table illustrates the number of universities ranked among the world’s top 200 in three subjects in five different countries in 2011.
Overall, the USA had the highest number of top-ranked universities in all three subjects, while New Zealand recorded the lowest figures in general. Psychology was the most prominent subject in Australia and Canada, whereas Biology ranked first in the USA and the UK.
To elaborate on this, regarding Biology, the USA ranked first, with 69 universities, more than double the figure for the United Kingdom, at 30. Australia and Canada shared the same number, at 9, while New Zealand recorded the lowest figure, at just 6. A similar pattern could be seen in Medicine, with the USA again leading at 54 universities, followed by the UK at 24. The figures for Australia and Canada were relatively similar, at 13 and 12, respectively, whereas New Zealand had only 2 universities in the top 200.
Regarding Psychology, the USA continued to record the highest figure, at 58 universities, followed by the UK, at 29. Australia ranked third, with 17 universities, while Canada had a slightly lower figure, at 14. New Zealand once again recorded the lowest number, at just 4. Notably, Psychology was the leading subject in both Australia and Canada, while Biology had the highest figure in the USA and the UK.

A similar pattern can be seen in Business, where University A charged $40,000, compared with $50,000 at University B and $60,000 at University C. Notably, University C had the highest fees for Business students, while University A generally had the lowest fees.
